statement: In the pooled ridge model on demand lags 1-4 and 4/13-week rolling means (alpha=1.0, yoy=false, log=false, trend=false, cat=false, clip=null, window=null, series_mean=false in BOTH arms, with naive inverse transforms and no bias corrections applied identically as a fixed post-hoc step to both arms and not treated as a model parameter), adding the known-in-advance count of promotion weeks in the forecast window as a feature (treatment: promo=true, all else as above) reduces next-4-week unit-sum WAPE by at least 1.0% relative to the identical specification with promo=false (comparator: promo is the sole difference from treatment; yoy remains false in the comparator, not true), as estimated by a two-way (series x rolling-origin) bootstrap under Design B (32 rolling origins, weeks 110-234, 260-week history).
kills_if: The two-way bootstrap 97.5% CI lower bound for the relative WAPE reduction (treatment vs comparator) is <= 1.0% (SESOI) -- drop the promo-count feature as implemented.
rationale: Locked to the judge's authoritative config: treatment and comparator are identical (lags 1-4, rolls 4/13, alpha=1.0, yoy=false, log=false, trend=false, cat=false, clip=null, window=null, series_mean=false) except promo=true vs promo=false. Clarification (1): the inverse transform and bias-correction choice ('naive', 'none') is a fixed, non-tunable step in the evaluation pipeline that converts model output back to unit-demand scale before WAPE is computed -- it is applied identically to both arms and is not a config/model parameter, so it does not and should not appear as a config key; because log=false in both arms here it reduces to the identity map, but the principle (uniform, untuned, post-hoc) holds regardless. Clarification (2): yoy=false in both treatment and comparator per the locked config -- the comparator is not a 'baseline without yoy' contrasted against a yoy-bearing treatment. Promo-count is the only difference between arms. The previously-discussed last-year-same-4-week-window feature (yoy=true) is a materially different, separate hypothesis with its own treatment/comparator pair and is not covered by this statement. Design B (32 origins) is chosen over A (6 origins, likely too few independent draws to resolve a SESOI-sized effect given promo weeks are sparse) and over C (58 origins, ~10x cost) as the minimum design expected to give the two-way bootstrap CI enough resolution at alpha=0.025 to distinguish a 2.5% target effect from the 1.0% SESOI. Establish the effect only if the CI lower bound exceeds 1.0%; otherwise kill, which subsumes CI-includes-zero and negative point-estimate cases.
